relations.note: Melinno poetically calls Roma the daughter of Ares.
Fate grants Roma lasting, unshaken sovereignty over nations.

relations.myth: Provincial joint cult of Roma and Augustus
relations.note: Augustus authorized provincial temples joining his worship with Roma's.
Roma sits beside the Jupiter-like enthroned Augustus as an equal imperial power.
Provincial coin types depict Roma crowning Augustus while holding a cornucopia.

relations.myth: Authorized eastern cult of Roma and Divus Julius
relations.note: Roman citizens in eastern provinces were permitted to honor Roma with Divus Julius.
Imperial images show Roma holding or receiving a small personified Victory.
Roma Aeterna and Venus Felix occupied opposed back-to-back cellae.
Roma holds the Trojan Palladium associated with Pallas, asserting Roman custody.

relations.myth: Roma Aeterna joined with solar imagery
relations.note: Solar symbolism makes Roma's duration coextensive with cosmic time.

relations.myth: Roma Aeterna joined with lunar imagery
relations.note: Lunar symbolism makes Roma's duration coextensive with cosmic time.

relations.myth: Roma and Romulus commemorate foundation and renewal
relations.note: Later coins place Roma and Romulus together in programs of foundation and renewal.
Coinage and art pair Roma with Constantinopolis as distinct imperial capital-personifications.

relations.myth: Roma participates in Jupiter's divine council
relations.note: Claudian places Roma within the literary divine world ruled by Jupiter.
